verdict.rationale: Oyster documents a real outbound webhook system: pushed events, a bearer-token secret you supply when configuring the webhook, automatic retries (up to 9 attempts over about 48 hours), and namespaced event names you can filter on. However, the only documented event is an expense approval, so payroll-processed, employee-onboarded and payment-failed events are unproven. missing for 10: documented payroll processed / employee onboarded / payment failed event types, an event catalog and payload schemas, independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can subscribe to payroll lifecycle events (payroll processed, employee onboarded, payment failed) via webhooks to drive downstream automations

citations.quote: Webhooks are a way of receiving information from the Oyster platform by getting it "pushed" to you, as opposed to continually making requests ("polling")
We will include the secret you provide here as an Authorization header (bearer token) in all webhooks we send to you, to prove they've come from the Oyster platform.
Oyster will automatically retry webhook delivery up to 9 total attempts over approximately 48 hours
This will allow you to filter for only the events you care about.
